approved.label: Chlorophyll and cyanobacteria
approved.definition: Chlorophyll absorbs red light near 665 nm and fluoresces near 680 nm, and dense blooms reflect a peak near 710 nm. Cyanobacteria add phycocyanin absorption near 620 nm.

approved.label: Turbidity and suspended sediment
approved.definition: Suspended particles raise reflectance and move the reflectance maximum from green toward red and near-infrared wavelengths. Single red or near-infrared bands track suspended sediment.

checks.reason: Fetched Topp et al. 2020 Section 2.2. Total Suspended Solids: the sentence on the spectral maximum moving from 550 nm into red/NIR wavelengths, citation [49], appears verbatim across the page break.

approved.label: Dissolved organic matter
approved.definition: Colored dissolved organic matter, also called yellow matter, absorbs blue and green light. Absorption rises exponentially toward shorter wavelengths, so retrievals ratio red against green or blue.

checks.reason: Fetched Gholizadeh, Melesse and Reddi 2016 (PMC5017463) Section 4.2 Colored Dissolved Organic Matters (CDOM): the quoted sentence on reflectance below ~500 nm appears verbatim. Soomets et al. 2020 Table 1 independently ties CDOM to the same wavelengths used across the bands citing it.

approved.label: Surface temperature
approved.definition: Thermal infrared bands measure emitted radiant heat, which gives the radiant temperature of the water surface. Clouds block the measurement.

checks.reason: Fetched Gholizadeh et al. 2016 Section 4.6 Water Temperature: the quoted sentence on thermal infrared bands and radiant temperature appears verbatim.

approved.label: Atmospheric correction and screening
approved.definition: Aerosol, water vapor, cirrus, cloud, and sun glint add signal that a water retrieval must remove or mask. Absorption bands and near and shortwave infrared bands estimate these terms.

approved.definition: Water absorbs near-infrared and shortwave infrared light and appears dark where land is bright. Green to infrared indices such as NDWI and MNDWI separate water from land.

limitations: Topp et al. 2020 and Vanhellemont and Ruddick 2015 PDFs could not be read by WebFetch directly (it reported encoded/binary content); both were converted to text with pdftotext from the same binary WebFetch had already fetched and saved, then checked by exact string search. Vanhellemont 2023's PDF exceeded WebFetch's 10 MB limit and was fetched separately with curl, then converted with pdftotext.

The Landsat Collection 2 Level 3 DSWE Algorithm Description Document (PDF) could not be read by WebFetch directly; it was converted with pdftotext from the binary WebFetch had already fetched and saved, then checked by exact string search.

usgs.gov returns an HTTP 403 from CloudFront to direct curl requests, so the USGS Landsat 9 page, band-designation FAQ, and best-bands FAQ were read only through WebFetch, not cross-checked against raw HTML the way SentiWiki, MODIS, PMC, and Planet pages were. Three separate WebFetch calls to these pages were internally consistent with each other and with the draft's numbers.

Planet's PSScene Product Specification PDF (src-planet-psscene-spec) sits behind a Widen viewer with a signed, expiring link; both WebFetch and curl returned only viewer chrome (a title tag and UI text), never the document's own text, confirming the draft's own disclosed limitation. No band's or sensor's approved values depend solely on this source: every PlanetScope band table and range value it supposedly backs is also on developers.planet.com (redirects to docs.planet.com), which was independently read and matched the draft exactly. The one sentence that could not be found on any reachable page is PlanetScope's note that PSB.SD's nadir ground sample distance is 3.7-4.2 m and that orthorectified products use a 3.0 m pixel size; docs.planet.com states only a fleet-wide '3 m spatial resolution', which is what the per-band resolution_m: 3 values rest on and which is confirmed.

developers.planet.com/docs/data/planetscope/ and landsat.gsfc.nasa.gov/satellites/landsat-9/ both now return HTTP 301 redirects (to docs.planet.com/data/imagery/planetscope/ and science.nasa.gov/mission/landsat-9). Both redirect targets carry the same content the draft cites, read and confirmed at the new addresses.

Two locator strings point to the wrong subsection, though the quotes they cite are verbatim on the cited page and the checks that depend on them still hold: Soomets et al. 2020's 705 nm/Table 4 sentence (cited for Sentinel-2 B05, OLCI Oa11, and PlanetScope B7 turbidity) sits in the paper's Section 4 'Discussion', not Section 5 (Section 5 is 'Conclusions'). Vanhellemont 2023's glint sentence (cited for PlanetScope B8 correction) sits in Section 4 'Conclusions', not a 'Section 4 Discussion' (the paper combines results and discussion into Section 3 and has no separate Discussion section).

OLCI Oa16's turbidity use quotes Soomets Table 1's Multispectral Instrument (MSI) column TSM formula ('R783 - R740 + R865/2') rather than the Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) column's own formula for the same row ('R779 - R754 + R865/2'), even though Oa16 is an OLCI band; Oa12's turbidity use correctly cites the OLCI column for the same table row. Both formulas' wavelengths fall inside Oa16's 771.25-786.25 nm range, so the use still holds and no value changed, but the locator's column label does not describe this band's own instrument.

Sentinel-2A, Sentinel-3A/3B, and PlanetScope PSB.SD launch/start dates were confirmed against SentiWiki and Planet pages but not against an independent third-party source; they were internally consistent with well-established public mission dates.
